answer.generated: The optimal mini-batch size for a GPU with 256 cores is typically a power of 2, such as 256 itself, to fully exploit the parallelism available in the GPU. This size aligns with the degree of parallelism, ensuring that each of the 256 cores can be efficiently utilized in parallel computations. When training a neural network using Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), the dataset is randomly partitioned into mini-batches of 256 elements, which are then distributed across the cores. Each core processes a portion of the batch, contributing to the collective gradient calculation. This parallel processing significantly accelerates the training process by leveraging the high throughput of the GPU, thereby reducing the overall training time. The efficient distribution of work among cores minimizes idle time and maximizes resource utilization, highlighting the critical relationship between the degree of parallelism and the effective implementation of parallel algorithms on GPUs.
